title: Is It a Subsequence?

concept.title: Two pointers that only move forward
body: A word `s` is a **subsequence** of `t` if you can delete some letters of `t` (maybe none) and get `s`. The letters of `s` must appear in `t` in the same order, but not next to each other.
Go through `t` once. Whenever the current letter is the one `s` is waiting for, move on to the next letter of `s`. If every letter of `s` was found, it is a subsequence.

statement: You are given two words `s` and `t`. Print `yes` if `s` is a subsequence of `t`, otherwise print `no`.

examples.note: Delete b and d from abcde.
e comes after c in t, so the order is wrong.

hints: Keep an index `i` into `s`: the next letter you are waiting for.
Walk through `t`; when the letter equals `s[i]`, add one to `i`.
If `i` reached the length of `s`, the answer is yes.

starter.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

# Your code here

explanation: One pass over `t` while waiting for the next letter of `s`. The answer is yes when all letters of `s` were matched.

code.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

i = 0
for ch in t:
    if i < len(s) and ch == s[i]:
        i += 1
print("yes" if i == len(s) else "no")
